clue.text: Moved en masse from fighting in southern Mediterranean

indicators.note: the fighting sits inside the pair of letters for southern Mediterranean

parts.note: fighting is war

explanation.surface: Troops moving en masse away from a battle in the southern Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees or crowds that move together as a dense mass are said to have done so in a swarm.

clue.text: Band bare all and leave at last

parts.note: to bare all is to strip naked

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word leave

explanation.surface: An instruction to a band member to undress completely and then go home.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a narrow band of colour, as on a flag or a shirt.

clue.text: In America, a gun each

parts.note: piece is American slang for a handgun, which is why the clue says In America

explanation.surface: A remark that in the USA everyone carries a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In America' qualifies the slang: PIECE for a gun is chiefly American.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for each one, as in 'a pound apiece'.

clue.text: Names sit awkwardly, keeping credit for offenders

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the credit abbreviation within them
awkwardly says the letters of names sit are to be arranged clumsily into a new order

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Names placed uncomfortably on a list that takes in credit for wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit' reads as a verb in the surface but is just fodder; 'awkwardly' makes MISEANTS from it and 'keeping' signals the credit abbreviation going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscreants are wrongdoers or villains, so offenders is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Drinks in one area of rolling hills

definitions.meaning: to drink something quickly is to knock it back, gulp it
chalk uplands of southern England such as the South ..., an area of gentle grassy hills

explanation.surface: Someone having a drink in a hilly part of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Downs are the rolling chalk hills of southern England, as in the South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is gulps down a drink; the noun sense is rolling upland country.

clue.text: Approximate in weight, and forged

indicators.note: in says the word for approximate sits inside the abbreviation for weight

parts.note: a rough estimate is an approximate one

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's metal, roughly weighed and hammered into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrought iron is worked or shaped by hammering, which is what forging means.

clue.text: Mystery perplexed Hindu town

indicators.note: perplexed suggests confusion, so the letters of hindu town are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzle that baffles an Indian town.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunnit is a detective story, a mystery in which the culprit is revealed at the end.

clue.text: Witches needing no lid for this cooker

indicators.note: a lid sits on top, so in a down entry the top letter of the witches' word is removed

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: Witches who need no lid on their cauldron or cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the enclosed part of a cooker used for baking and roasting.

clue.text: Waterfowl work on good fruit

parts.note: a goose is a waterfowl
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Ducks and geese working on some good fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: GOOSEGOG is a British colloquial word for a gooseberry.
explanation.definitionFit: Goosegog is an informal British name for the gooseberry, a sour green berry.

clue.text: Composition needing delicacy is English

parts.note: a delicacy is a treat

explanation.surface: A piece of music or writing that needs a fine touch and is English.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written work on a subject, a type of composition.

clue.text: Helps to chase runs and attacks

indicators.note: one chases by following behind, so the helping word comes after the runs letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
helps means aids

explanation.surface: Helpers pursuing runners in some assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Raids are sudden attacks, as by troops or police on a target.

clue.text: The majority of ladies must accept predicaments can be healthy

indicators.note: must accept says the shortened word takes the predicaments inside it
the majority of a word is all but its last letter, so the word for ladies loses its end

parts.note: ladies are women
to be in a hole is to be in a predicament, so holes are predicaments

explanation.surface: Most women must put up with tricky situations to stay well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The majority of' leaves WOME, a trimmed synonym rather than letters printed in the clue; 'must accept' then signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome food or living is good for you, promoting good health.

clue.text: Irritation includes concerns for this literary form

indicators.note: includes says the word for irritation contains the word for concerns

parts.note: pique is resentment or irritation
concerns are cares

explanation.surface: A writer's annoyance that brings worries into a genre.
explanation.definitionFit: The picaresque is a genre of fiction following the episodic adventures of a roguish hero.

clue.text: Reacted emotionally to such material

definitions.meaning: to have sensed something or been moved by it
a matted woollen fabric made by pressing fibres together

explanation.surface: Someone moved by a particular fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of feel means experienced an emotion; the noun is a pressed woollen cloth.

clue.text: Plague caused by coppers covering steps in field

indicators.note: covering means the coins word wraps round the steps word

parts.note: coppers are low-value copper coins, pennies, so pence
a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a field fence

explanation.surface: A plague brought by policemen covering a field's steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins, PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilence is a deadly epidemic disease, the bubonic plague being the classic case.

clue.text: Grouchy old American chasing tin vessel

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so old American comes after tin vessel

parts.note: a tin is a can
a tanker is a ship, a vessel
US stands for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A grumpy elderly Yank running after a tin boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means bad-tempered and argumentative, which grouchy also means.

clue.text: Criminal here to use superior accommodation

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters of here to use are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook here to use luxury lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' is meant literally: the accommodation is up high in the branches, not posh.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling built among branches is literally above ground level, so it is accommodation set higher up.

clue.text: Away and certain to be heard — not far from the coast

parts.note: off means away, as in 'I'm off'

indicators.note: to be heard says the word for certain is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Someone who has gone, sure to be audible, near the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore describes waters at sea but within sight of land, a short distance out.

clue.text: Go with son and tip up cooker on fire

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word tip is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A son told to overturn a burning stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit is a rotating spit for roasting meat over an open fire.

clue.text: Just out of the medals facing Spain, say the press

parts.note: fourth place is just behind bronze, missing a medal
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
to say is to state

explanation.surface: An athlete just missing a medal and facing Spain makes a comment.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is a traditional name for journalists and the press as a political force.

clue.text: A struggle to pack a ton and fly

indicators.note: to pack means the struggle word has letters stuffed inside it

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: It is a struggle to load a heavy weight and take off.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot an aircraft, a formal word for flying.

clue.text: Likely to win strange spoon, oddly

parts.note: strange means odd

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, of the word spoon

explanation.surface: A weird spoon, strangely, set to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is odds-on is so favoured that a bet pays less than the stake, so it should win.

clue.text: Evil king's ruin

parts.note: evil is sin, wickedness
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A wicked monarch's downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink a plan or a person is to ruin them, scupper them.

clue.text: Ephemeral spirit Old Nick rejected

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the name for the Devil is read backwards

parts.note: Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil

explanation.surface: A fleeting ghost that the Devil turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses DEVIL to LIVED. 'spirit' looks ghostly but is a drink: a SHORT is a measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral things last only a brief time, so they do not survive long.

clue.text: Raise charge in case of rapids or rocks

indicators.note: in says the lifted charge goes inside the outer letters of rapids
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters
raise means lift up, so in a down entry the charge word is read upwards

parts.note: a charge is a fee

explanation.surface: Raising the price of a ride through rapids or rocky water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' gives EEF in this down entry, and 'case of' takes only the outside letters of rapids; 'in' joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefs are ridges of rock or coral lying near the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Encourage rapid growth, ignoring head

indicators.note: ignoring head means the word for rapid growth loses its first letter

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rapid increase

explanation.surface: Advice to promote fast growth without thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press or spur them on, to encourage.

clue.text: Suitable work left on board with a Parisienne

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship, as seen on board
une is French for a, in the feminine form a Parisian woman would use

explanation.surface: Good work left on a ship with a woman from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or convenient, suitable for the occasion.

clue.text: Within earshot, guarding approaches

indicators.note: guarding says the words within earshot hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Someone nearby, keeping watch as others come close.
explanation.definitionFit: Nears is a verb meaning comes closer to, so it matches approaches.

clue.text: Furthest from the centre — and high in intensity

definitions.meaning: situated at the outermost point, the farthest edge
very great or severe in degree

explanation.surface: Something at the outer edge and also very intense.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means both outermost in position and very great in degree.

clue.text: The girl has gone for a drink here!

parts.note: the girl is she
been means gone and come back, as in 'she has been to Dublin'

explanation.surface: A woman has popped out to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an illicit drinking den, chiefly Irish and Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an unlicensed bar, a place where people go to drink.
